methodological_rigor.justification: Phase 1 trial with appropriate 3+3 dose escalation design followed by disease-specific expansion cohorts. Clear primary objectives (safety, tolerability) and secondary objectives. Comprehensive inclusion/exclusion criteria with detailed IRB oversight and data monitoring committee established. Limitations acknowledged including small sample sizes and patient pre-treatment burden, though baseline characteristics well documented across parts A1, A2, and B.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Phase 1 trial evaluating novel mechanism (selective TGFβ1 inhibition) in clinically important population (anti-PD-1-resistant advanced solid tumors). Directly addresses unmet clinical need in ICI-resistant disease. Biomarker analyses (CD8+ T cell, Treg, TGFβ1) provide mechanistic understanding and potential patient selection strategy. Combination approach with pembrolizumab shows clinical activity (20% ORR in ccRCC) in heavily pretreated patients with poor prognosis.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT diagram clearly presented; comprehensive safety and efficacy tables with detailed adverse event grading; methods section specifies statistical approaches (Clopper-Pearson for ORRs, Kaplan-Meier curves). Data availability statement indicates Nature Portfolio reporting summary available but specific data/code availability not detailed in manuscript. Limited statement on replication materials.

novelty_literature.justification: First-in-human phase 1 trial of linavonkibart, a novel first-in-class selective anti-latent TGFβ1 antibody. Addresses demonstrated gap: selective TGFβ1 inhibition intended to overcome cardiotoxicity of pan-TGFβ inhibitors while maintaining efficacy. Combination with anti-PD-1 in established ICI-resistant patient population represents novel therapeutic strategy with preclinical support.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear structure: comprehensive Methods section detailing study design, patient eligibility, assessments, and statistical analysis; Results systematically presented by study part with supporting tables and figures (CONSORT, swimmer/spider/waterfall plots, biomarker data); Discussion connects findings to preclinical evidence and clinical implications. Figure captions provide adequate detail.

key_strengths: First-in-human phase 1 trial of novel selective TGFβ1 inhibitor with strong mechanistic rationale and preclinical support for addressing ICI resistance
Favorable safety profile with no dose-limiting toxicities and manageable adverse event profile, distinguishing from prior pan-TGFβ approaches
Promising clinical activity in heavily pretreated, poor-prognosis ccRCC cohort (20% ORR) with biomarker-driven patient selection strategy showing enhanced responses
Comprehensive immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry analyses demonstrating mechanism of action (increased CD8+ infiltration, reduced Treg/CD8 ratio, MDSC suppression)
Well-structured phase 1 design with appropriate dose escalation, expansion cohorts, and rigorous safety monitoring via data review committee
key_concerns: Small sample sizes across all cohorts limit definitive efficacy conclusions; expansion cohorts based on Bayesian monitoring rather than powered sample size calculations
Single-arm trial design precludes direct comparison to best supportive care or continued monotherapy; historical controls acknowledge but do not eliminate bias
Heavily pretreated patient population (median 3 prior lines, 38.5% with ≥2 prior anti-PD-1 lines) may confound true drug efficacy by selecting for chemotherapy-refractory population
Biomarker cutoff values (CD8+ ≥5%, Treg ≥0.3%, TGFβ1 ≥50%) determined empirically on small subsets (n=16 biopsies) without prospective validation
Limited follow-up data collection; median treatment duration 13.8 months with incomplete long-term outcome maturity
chief_reviewer.rationale: Phase 1 trial demonstrates solid methodology, novel mechanism, and promising early signals in difficult-to-treat population. Appropriate for Tier 2 (10-19 JIF) journals as methodologically sound work with clear translational contribution but requiring phase 2 validation. Minor revisions would address sample size limitations and biomarker validation plans.
